message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (a jerk) for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my brother and I live with our parents. He's 30 and went back to school after being in a bad job, which is why he moved back in about 11 months ago. I'm 21, in my third year of university, working to put myself through school, and studying business. I'm finding it difficult but manageable, and I should graduate in two years. When I started university, I began saving a bit from all my paycheques. Sometimes it was as much as 15%, other times as low as 1%, but I've managed to save about $2800 so far. My plan is to go on a big vacation after graduation, probably a cruise or a trip to Japan or Europe, places I've never been to. My brother hasn't been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. Our parents already help him financially, so he wouldn't ask them for more help for that. Last week, when he was complaining to my parents about not being able to go on a vacation, they mentioned me and my vacation fund, suggesting that he could have been doing something similar all these years to afford a trip, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. Three days ago, my brother came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or fall. He said since I won't need it for another two years, there's plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. Now, my brother is really mad at me. He says it's not fair because, as the youngest child, I get to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He also says it's not fair that I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went, whereas he had to go back. He even says I've only been able to save so much money because mom and dad spoiled me. I disagree with him. My father, as well as my university accounting and finance classes, taught me to budget. If anything, I think my parents spoiled him because he doesn't know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don't think it's fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I also doubt he'll be able to pay me back in time, even if he could. I'm feeling uncomfortable about this whole situation. Am I being AITA for refusing to loan him my vacation money? Okay, so to break this down, I need to consider several factors: 1. **Financial Responsibility**: Am I being responsible by saving for my own future vacation, or am I being selfish by not helping my brother? 2. **Family Dynamics**: How do our family roles and past experiences influence our current conflict? 3. **Brother's Financial Situation**: Is my brother in a position to pay me back, or is he likely to default on the loan? 4. **Emotional Impact**: How does this decision affect our relationship, and am I okay with the potential fallout? 5. **Alternative Solutions**: Are there other ways to help my brother without sacrificing my own plans? Let me think about each of these points. **1. Financial Responsibility**: I've been saving diligently for my vacation, which is a significant goal for me. By refusing to loan him the money, I'm prioritizing my own financial goals. However, some might argue that helping family in need is also a responsible thing to do. **2. Family Dynamics**: My brother feels that I've had more opportunities and support from our parents, which has allowed me to save money. He feels that he's had to work harder and make sacrifices, which is why he's now in a difficult financial spot. This sense of unfairness is making him angry. **3. Brother's Financial Situation**: My brother is not good with money. He makes about the same as I do, but he's always broke despite not paying rent or buying groceries. This makes me doubt his ability to pay me back, even if he promises to. **4. Emotional Impact**: Refusing to help him is causing tension in our relationship. He's upset, and this could lead to long-term resentment or a strained relationship. **5. Alternative Solutions**: Instead of loaning him the money, maybe I can find other ways to help him save or earn more. For example, helping him create a budget or find additional income sources. However, this requires his cooperation, which he might not be willing to give given his current anger. Considering all these factors, I need to decide whether refusing to loan him the money is justified or if I'm being too rigid. On one hand, I've worked hard to save this money, and it's for a goal that I've been looking forward to. On the other hand, my brother is in need, and as family, it's natural to want to help each other out. But given his history of poor money management and the likelihood that he might not be able to pay me back, it seems risky to lend him the money. Plus, I don't want to compromise my own plans and goals. However, I also don't want to damage our relationship. Maybe there's a middle ground where I can help him in a way that doesn't jeopardize my savings. For example, maybe we can discuss his financial situation and find ways for him to save on his own, or perhaps we can plan a cheaper vacation together. But given the current situation, where he's insisting on borrowing my money and I'm not comfortable with that, it might be best to stick to my decision and explain my reasoning calmly. It's important to communicate my concerns and why I can't lend him the money, while also expressing that I care about his well-being. In conclusion, while it's tough, I think refusing to loan him the money is the right decision for me, given my financial goals and his history of poor money management.
